hero.subtitle: Your agent opens a payment channel and pays for every call, every token, in milliseconds, without touching the chain. The seller settles thousands of payments in a single transaction. How much the agent can spend, and with whom, is decided by its account on Stellar, not by a server.

playground.disclaimer: Simulation: runs in your browser and makes no network requests. Rules, prices and reason codes match the product; on-chain steps are shown as ≈5 s instead of actually waiting.
playground.chatText: Every ledger on Stellar closes in about five seconds. That is quick for a single payment, but far too slow if you want to pay for every call or every token on its own. That is why payment channels exist. The agent opens a channel once and locks a deposit in the contract. From then on, each request carries a signed, cumulative voucher that never touches the chain. The seller checks it in milliseconds, answers right away, and settles whatever has built up in one transaction whenever it likes. Because vouchers are cumulative, the seller only keeps the latest one; an old voucher can never be worth more. When the deposit runs out, the stream stops, even in the middle of a sentence. The spending limit lives in the agent's account. The chain, not a server, enforces the daily cap, the per-transaction cap and the list of allowed payees. Even a compromised agent cannot send funds to its own wallet, because that address is not on the list. The facilitator pays network fees, verifies vouchers and triggers settlement on time, but it cannot touch the money. Anyone can verify a voucher, and funds only ever go to the channel's seller. So a thousand payments fit into two transactions: one to open the channel and one to settle it. You give your agent the keys. You keep the reins.

problem.title: Agents are spending money. The rails aren't ready.
problem.subtitle: Today's x402 flow turns every payment into its own transaction. Too slow for fast calls, too costly for tiny amounts, too blunt for permissions.

steps.title: Put on the reins
steps.body: The owner sets up a {name} Account: a daily cap, a per-transaction cap and a list of allowed sellers. The rules are written on-chain.

steps.title: Open the channel
steps.body: The agent opens a channel with the seller in one transaction and locks a deposit. The deposit counts against the daily cap, so a channel can't break the limit.

steps.title: Pay, stream, settle
steps.body: Every request carries a signed, cumulative voucher that the seller checks in milliseconds. It all settles in one transaction, and whatever is left goes back to the agent.

architecture.title: The facilitator can't touch the money.
architecture.subtitle: Anyone can verify a voucher, and anyone can trigger settlement. Funds only ever go to the channel's seller.

items.name: {name} Account
items.body: Holds the funds and enforces the daily cap, the per-transaction cap and the allowed payees. A transfer that breaks the rules is rejected on-chain.

items.name: Channel contract
items.body: Locks the deposit, verifies the cumulative voucher, settles and refunds. Because vouchers are cumulative, double spending is structurally impossible.

items.name: Facilitator
items.body: Verifies vouchers, triggers settlement automatically before the channel expires, and pays network fees. It has no authority to withdraw funds.

items.q: Do I have to trust the facilitator?
items.a: No. Vouchers are verified by the channel contract, and funds only go to the channel's seller. The facilitator verifies, triggers settlement and pays network fees; it can't withdraw anything.

items.q: What if the channel closes before the seller settles?
items.a: The agent can only close the channel after it expires and a grace period passes. The facilitator settles automatically before that happens.

items.q: Can the agent spend more than its deposit?
items.a: No. A voucher above the deposit is rejected by both the facilitator and the chain (CHANNEL_EXHAUSTED), and the stream stops mid-sentence.

items.q: Can the agent move funds to its own wallet?
items.a: No. The {name} Account only pays allowed payees, and the chain enforces it (PAYEE_NOT_ALLOWED).

items.q: Does the agent need to hold XLM?
items.a: No. The facilitator pays network fees.
Custom account auth (__check_auth), fee sponsorship and very low transaction costs. Together they make on-chain spending limits and cheap channel opens and settlements possible.
No. It's a payment rail with spending permissions. Agents use it to pay whatever service they need.

meter.codeTitle: Your first paid endpoint in 60 seconds
meter.codeLead: Install the package, pass the facilitator URL and your Stellar address, set a price. The 402 response, voucher verification and settlement come built in.
meter.responseLead: Agents don't read docs. The 402 body states the price, unit, network and pay-to address in a machine-readable shape; @reinkey/sdk handles the rest.

features.title: Three units
features.body: request: per call. token: slice by slice on a streamed response. second: for exactly as long as a live feed is listened to. Payment stops when the connection drops; the stream stops when the deposit runs out. All three in one package; rk.stream() for streams.

features.title: Non-custodial
features.body: Funds sit either in the buyer's account or in the channel contract. The facilitator can't touch them: anyone can verify a voucher, anyone can trigger settlement, and the money only goes to you.

features.title: Automatic settlement
features.body: Once accumulated vouchers pass a threshold, or the channel nears expiry, the facilitator settles with a single claim transaction. Don't want to wait? Trigger it yourself: anyone can call claim.

features.title: Standard x402
features.body: PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and PAYMENT-RESPONSE are the same headers as x402 v2. The channel scheme is offered next to exact as a second option.

features.title: No network fees
features.body: Buyers don't need to hold XLM; the facilitator pays transaction fees. You only ever receive USDC.

features.title: Explainable rejections
features.body: Every rejected payment returns a reason code: CHANNEL_EXHAUSTED, VOUCHER_UNDERPAID, WRONG_PAYEE, CHANNEL_EXPIRING. The agent reads what to fix from the body; nobody opens a support ticket.

meta.title: Reins: on-chain spending authority for agents
meta.description: Give your agent the keys, keep the reins. Daily cap, per-transaction cap, allowed payees and trading pairs are written on Stellar and enforced by the network.

reins.title: The agent holds the key. You hold the reins.
reins.tagline: An agent account whose limits are enforced by the chain, not a server.
reins.subtitle: Reins is a smart account with its policy written on-chain. The agent pays and trades with its own key; Stellar enforces the cap, the allowed payees and the allowed pairs. Even a stolen key can't step outside the limit.
bullets: Allowed payees and trading pairs only
Freeze in one transaction, recall in one transaction
reins.codeLead: The agent opens a channel in one transaction, then pays for every call with a signed voucher. No sign-up, no API key, no credit card.
reins.responseLead: The rejection comes from __check_auth, not from a server: with a transaction hash and a reason code anyone can verify.

features.title: Policy on-chain
features.body: Daily cap, per-transaction cap, allowed payees, allowed DEX pairs and an expiry are written inside the account. The limit holds even if a server goes down or gets compromised.

features.title: Freeze and recall
features.body: The owner freezes the account in one transaction: from that moment the agent key can't sign anything. recall pulls the balance back whenever you want.

features.title: Bounded trading
features.body: The agent can trade on the Stellar DEX (Soroswap); which pair, how much per trade and per day is in the policy. Trades without slippage protection are rejected. With no USDC on hand, a channel opens with XLM: just enough is converted on the DEX and the seller still receives USDC.

features.title: No XLM for the agent
features.body: A relayer submits the transaction and pays the fee; the agent only signs the authorization entry. The only asset in the agent's wallet is USDC.

features.title: Explainable rejections
features.body: Every rejection carries a reason code: PER_TX_CAP_EXCEEDED, PAYEE_NOT_ALLOWED, DAILY_CAP_EXCEEDED, ACCOUNT_FROZEN. Policy rejections also surface in simulation, before anything hits the chain.

features.title: Live audit
features.body: The console shows every payment, every on-chain transaction and every rejection live; the permanent ledger is paginated and complete.

reins.limitsTitle: What exists today, and what doesn't
limits: Runs on Stellar testnet; the contracts haven't been audited yet.
Accounts are deployed with a script today; one-click setup from the console is on the roadmap.
On-chain trade limits apply on the DEX side. The chain can't see trades inside a centralized exchange's internal ledger.
reins.ctaTitle: Give your agent spending power, safely.

meta.title: Float: uncollateralized working capital for agents
meta.description: Once an agent's account is handed to the pool, funds can't leave its policy. Capital that can't escape needs no collateral: investors deposit USDC, agents work on credit, health is computed on-chain.

float.title: Capital that can't escape needs no collateral.
float.tagline: Working capital for agents. Risk is computed on-chain.
float.subtitle: Funds in a Reins account can only go where its policy allows. Once the account is handed to the pool, even its owner's signature stops working: neither the agent nor whoever created the account can take the credit out. Float is a lending pool built on that property.
bullets: Investors deposit USDC and receive shares
Agents pay and trade on an uncollateralized line
Anyone can liquidate once value falls below the threshold
float.codeTitle: The pool is a public API
float.codeLead: Size, share price, utilization and investor positions are read from the chain. Share price = (idle USDC + outstanding debt + pool XLM × price) / total shares.
float.responseTitle: Every line's health is computed on-chain
float.responseLead: Value is the account's USDC plus its XLM at a conservative price. Below 90% of debt, anyone can trigger liquidation: the account is frozen, remaining funds return to the pool, and the loss shows up in the share price.

features.title: Capital that can't escape
features.body: Credit is transferred into a Reins account and control of the account passes to the pool (set_controller). The policy only allows payments to approved sellers and swaps on approved pairs; money can't leave the system.

features.title: Conservative pricing
features.body: Valuation uses the lower of the oracle (Reflector) and the DEX pool price. Pumping the DEX price can't make an account look healthy.

features.title: Permissionless liquidation
features.body: Anyone can call liquidate. The condition is checked on-chain; a healthy account cannot be liquidated.

features.title: Profit sharing
features.body: When a line closes, debt returns to the pool, a share of the profit (20% today) goes to the pool and the rest to the beneficiary. Every profitable line raises the share price.

features.title: Shares are a claim
features.body: An investor's shares are a transferable balance worth shares × share price. Withdrawals are limited to the USDC sitting idle in the pool.

features.title: Live visibility
features.body: The console's Float view shows pool size, share-price history, utilization and a health gauge for every line, live.

float.limitsTitle: What exists today, and what doesn't
limits: Runs on Stellar testnet; the contract hasn't been audited. Don't deposit real capital.
The console and API are read-only today: depositing, opening a line and liquidating are contract calls with no UI. Opening a line is the admin's decision; there is no permissionless borrowing.

Unspent deposits in open channels aren't counted in health (an error on the cautious side). With only the DEX price source configured, the price can be moved by a single large trade; mainnet needs the oracle and a TWAP.
